dissents.topic: Severity of feature overlap between value_to_metric and detailed_metric

positions.position: P1 — wrong data structure; both flags express the same idea and should be unified into one per-descriptor enum/bool rather than two overlapping flags with a precedence rule.
P1 — feature overlaps without a clear conceptual line; should have asked first whether detailed_metric should grow a per-level scope rather than introducing a second partially-overlapping flag.
P2 — overlap is real and worth pushing back on before the API surface freezes, but not a blocker; a single per-descriptor enum (none|key_only|key_and_value) would be cleaner.
Did not flag the overlap as a standalone issue, though Liskov flagged the related precedence-composition concern.

dissents.topic: Whether the per-entry three-branch metric builder collapses to a single rule

positions.position: Branches collapse to ~3 lines: write key; if (valueToMetric || matchedUsingValue) && value != "", write _value. The wildcard/matchedUsingValue/default distinctions never change the output.
Three branches reduce to one rule: 'write key; if valueToMetric and value!="" then write _value' — wildcard branch is identical to default+valueToMetric branch.
Five interleaved arms collapse to one predicate: append key, append _value iff (flag OR matchedUsingValue) AND value != "". Same conclusion as Pike.
Same collapse via `includeValue := nextDescriptor.valueToMetric || matchedUsingValue`; current shape is a smuggled-goto via flags.
Agrees branches do nearly the same work and should be one helper, but frames the rule slightly differently — extract a helper rather than necessarily collapsing to a single expression.

Frames the duplication at a higher level — two parallel key builders (detailedMetricFullKey and valueToMetricFullKey) that will drift; wants one policy-parameterized builder, not just the inner collapse.

dissents.topic: Whether the nil-nextDescriptor branch's append of entry.Key is dead/harmful

positions.position: P2 — comment 'still append something deterministic' admits author was unsure; either prove load-bearing or delete.
P1 — dead code in a hot path is a smell; correctness, not determinism, is the property wanted.
P1 — no test covers this branch; unclear if intentional or leftover from detailed_metric; either drop the segment or add a test and comment.
P2 — write has no observable effect and muddies the invariant; either document or remove.
Did not flag this branch explicitly.

issues.description: GetLimit mutates shared *RateLimit from the config tree, racing across concurrent requests with different runtime values
issues.detail: rateLimit is the pointer stored in the descriptor tree (set by loadDescriptors) and is shared across all callers. The new code writes rateLimit.Stats = NewStats(enhancedKey) and rateLimit.FullKey = enhancedKey on every call, with a per-request key. Concurrent GetLimit calls on the same leaf with different entry values will race on Stats/FullKey, and one request's increment can land on another request's counter. The pre-existing detailed_metric branch had the same shape but a stable key; value_to_metric turns the latent hazard into a guaranteed bug. Fix by returning a per-call copy (or a (RateLimit, statsKey) pair) rather than mutating the shared object.

issues.description: Unbounded stats cardinality: raw runtime values written into stats keys with no cap, sanitization, or memoization
issues.detail: value_to_metric concatenates entry.Value directly into the metric key via NewStats(enhancedKey) on every request, with no length cap, allowed-character set, cardinality bound, or lookup-before-create. Runtime values like subject_id, route, or wildcard-matched action are exactly the user-controlled high-cardinality strings that produce a DoS / memory-growth vector. detailed_metric carries an explicit NB warning about this; value_to_metric inherits the hazard but is marketed as the lower-cardinality alternative. Cap key length, restrict charset, memoize NewStats per key, and at minimum mirror detailed_metric's cardinality warning.

issues.description: Stats counter allocated twice on the override path; the first NewStats is orphaned
issues.detail: The post-loop branch calls NewRateLimit(... NewStats(rateLimit.FullKey) ...) and then immediately overwrites rateLimit.Stats with NewStats(enhancedKey). The first counter is registered under the old key and discarded one line later, leaking a stats handle on every request and creating ghost counters under the non-enhanced key. Either the reconstruction matters (then keep it without overwriting) or it does not (then delete it); as written it is dead allocation in a hot path.

issues.description: rateLimit pointer is reassigned to a per-request RateLimit inside GetLimit, breaking shared-state semantics
issues.detail: rateLimit came from nextDescriptor.limit — the canonical shared descriptor-tree pointer returned to every caller. The override branch does rateLimit = NewRateLimit(...), replacing the local pointer with a per-call object. All other code paths return the shared descriptor.limit; value_to_metric paths now return a fresh per-request RateLimit. Callers/tests relying on identity, on cross-request shared state, or on stats accumulation across requests will see divergent behavior between value_to_metric paths and every other path.

issues.description: Override condition `enhancedKey != rateLimit.FullKey` is the wrong predicate for the value_to_metric feature
issues.detail: The intended postcondition is: when an ancestor descriptor has value_to_metric:true and matched a runtime value, use the enhanced key; otherwise leave stats alone. The implemented guard asks whether two constructed strings differ. These are not the same predicate — the valueToMetric flag is never consulted at the decision site, the override can fire whenever the strings happen to differ for unrelated reasons, and a future change to how FullKey is built upstream could silently flip behavior. Additionally, if any descriptor's RateLimit was created with FullKey == "", the comparison is trivially true on every request, dragging value_to_metric==false descriptors into the reallocation path.

issues.description: Specification missing: value_to_metric semantics and the detailed_metric precedence rule are not stated as contracts
issues.detail: The README prose claims value_to_metric only affects descriptors where the value is not explicitly defined, and that detailed_metric takes precedence. But the code has three branches (wildcard, matchedUsingValue, default-key) crossed with (flag set, unset, detailed_metric set), and the matchedUsingValue arm appends the value regardless of value_to_metric, contradicting the README. The precedence guard uses rateLimit.DetailedMetric (the leaf's flag) — behavior with detailed_metric on an intermediate and value_to_metric on a leaf is undefined. The full precondition/postcondition table per branch needs to be written down before this lands.

issues.description: Three-way branch in the per-entry metric builder collapses to a single rule
issues.detail: The if matchedViaWildcard / else if matchedUsingValue / else block contains three arms that all reduce to: write key; if (nextDescriptor.valueToMetric || matchedUsingValue) AND value != "", append _value. Two of the three arms are textually identical. The structured form is one assignment to includeValue and one write. Writing it as five interleaved arms makes incidental complexity look essential and forces maintainers to diff three near-duplicate branches by hand.

issues.description: Two parallel key builders (detailedMetricFullKey and valueToMetricFullKey) duplicate traversal logic and will drift
issues.detail: GetLimit now maintains detailedMetricFullKey, valueToMetricFullKey, and rateLimit.FullKey side by side, each appending a per-level segment with overlapping rules. Any future change to descriptor matching must be mirrored in both builders. The right shape is a single metric-key builder parameterized by policy (off / detailed / value-to-metric / both), or a []segment of {key, value, includeValue} rendered once at the end. As written, it is copy-paste-for-reuse: two near-identical codepaths kept in sync by hand.

issues.description: Abstraction leak: per-request metric-key construction lives inside config-tree traversal
issues.detail: rateLimitConfigImpl's responsibility is resolving a descriptor tuple to a cached config node. The per-call enhanced metric key is a per-request concern. By writing the per-request key into rateLimit.FullKey and rateLimit.Stats — both fields of the cached node — the abstraction leaks per-call state into the config tree. The correct boundary is GetLimit returns (RateLimit, statsKey) or wraps the cached RateLimit in a per-call value. This conflation is what creates the mutation/race hazard above.

issues.description: Per-request strings.Builder allocation and NewStats calls on the hot path even when no descriptor uses value_to_metric
issues.detail: GetLimit is called on every rate-limit request. The new code unconditionally allocates a second strings.Builder and performs map lookups / counter registrations even when no descriptor in the config uses the feature. The fix is to gate the second builder behind a 'this subtree has any value_to_metric descriptor' boolean computed at config load time, so the cost is zero for configs that don't use the feature.

issues.description: Feature overlaps detailed_metric without a clear conceptual line — two flags answering the same question
issues.detail: detailed_metric means 'include runtime values in the metric key.' value_to_metric means 'include runtime values in the metric key, but selectively, with precedence rules.' Both flags express the same idea; the right shape is a single per-descriptor enum/bool (e.g., metric_value: none | key_only | key_and_value), with detailed_metric as the leaf-only special case. Instead, the PR ships a parallel field, parallel builder, parallel walk, and a precedence rule between two flags that mean the same thing — exactly how config files become unmaintainable.

issues.description: matchedUsingValue is a fragile mutable flag whose meaning depends on the order of later statements
issues.detail: matchedUsingValue := nextDescriptor != nil is set after the wildcard branch but before the default-key fallback, then cleared inside the fallback. A small refactor in the fallback would silently break the metric key. State the loop invariant ('matchedUsingValue is true iff descriptor was matched by explicit key+value') and use a switch over (wildcard, exact, default) or a matchKind enum instead of a mutable flag.

issues.description: valueToMetric flag is read from nextDescriptor rather than the parent — semantics subtle and undocumented
issues.detail: The flag affects how *this* level's segment is rendered but is read from nextDescriptor.valueToMetric (the child just matched). This is correct intent but undocumented, and interacts oddly when no child matches (nextDescriptor == nil), in which case the code falls through to key-only with no comment. The behavior when value_to_metric is set on a descriptor whose value matches an explicit key+value with empty configured Value is also untested.

issues.description: nil-nextDescriptor branch still appends entry.Key to the enhanced builder — dead or undocumented
issues.detail: When no descriptor matches, the code appends entry.Key to valueToMetricFullKey with a comment 'still append something deterministic.' If nextDescriptor is nil the loop typically exits and the builder result is unused; the append has no observable effect and muddies the 'builder reflects matched prefix' invariant. Either document why it is load-bearing (with a test) or delete it.

issues.description: valueToMetricFullKey invariant is not actually maintained across break paths
issues.detail: The for loop has multiple break paths (limit found, descriptor not found). valueToMetricFullKey is appended before those breaks but never trimmed afterward; in some paths it contains a trailing partial segment that is never read. The invariant 'valueToMetricFullKey corresponds to the matched prefix at the current iteration' is not enforced — it just happens to agree at the loop-exit iteration. State and maintain the invariant, or stop pretending to.

issues.description: FullKey semantics silently changed for the detailed_metric path
issues.detail: Previously the detailed-metric branch only updated rateLimit.Stats. This PR also writes rateLimit.FullKey = detailedKey, a behavior change for any caller that reads FullKey (logs, debug). The test TestValueToMetric_FullKeyMatchesStatsKey encodes the new invariant but the PR description does not call out the change or justify why the prior invariant was wrong. State FullKey == Stats.Key as a deliberate type-level invariant, or revert.

issues.description: Positional struct literals for rateLimitDescriptor make the new field invisible and fragile
issues.detail: &rateLimitDescriptor{map[string]*rateLimitDescriptor{}, rateLimit, nil, descriptorConfig.ValueToMetric} and the matching domain construction use positional initialization. Adding a fourth field already required touching both call sites; the fifth will be a footgun and could silently swap meanings if order shifts. Named-field initialization is a few tokens and removes the whole class of bug.

issues.description: Documentation under-states the cardinality risk that detailed_metric documents explicitly
issues.detail: The README's detailed_metric section warns 'this should only be enabled in situations where the potentially large cardinality of metrics that this can lead to is acceptable.' The new value_to_metric section omits that warning and frames the feature as a lower-cardinality alternative, even though cardinality is a property of the value space, not of which descriptors opt in. Mirror the warning, and note that values are not sanitized (so '.' or whitespace in values will affect downstream metric backends).

issues.description: Tests assert worked examples; the documented invariants and concurrency boundaries are not tested
issues.detail: All new tests are single-threaded happy-path I/O examples. None states the property: enhanced_key(d) = join(domain, segments(d)) where segment includes value iff includeValue holds. None exercises (a) concurrent GetLimit on the same descriptor with two different runtime values (would surface the shared-state race), (b) intermediate detailed_metric + leaf value_to_metric (the cross-feature precedence boundary), (c) value sanitization with '.', whitespace, non-ASCII, or extreme length, (d) high-cardinality cycling to confirm the stats store is bounded, (e) value_to_metric:true subtrees with no rate_limit at the leaf. Tests prove the formatting code is wired up; they do not prove the feature is safe.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges decisively on three P0 findings: (1) GetLimit mutates a shared *RateLimit pointer stored in the descriptor tree, with per-request runtime values overwriting Stats and FullKey — a guaranteed concurrency race under any QPS with varying values (flagged by all six reviewers); (2) NewStats is called per request with a key derived from unbounded user-controlled runtime values, with no cap, sanitization, or memoization, creating exactly the cardinality DoS the adjacent detailed_metric warning was written for (flagged by Knuth, Hickey, Torvalds, Dijkstra); (3) the override branch allocates a stats counter then immediately discards it, leaking a stats handle on every request and registering ghost counters under the old key (Knuth, Torvalds, Pike, Dijkstra). All five non-Hickey reviewers also independently observe that the three-arm per-entry branch collapses to a single rule (`includeValue := nextDescriptor.valueToMetric || matchedUsingValue`). The strongest preserved disagreement is over how to resolve the overlap with detailed_metric: Pike says it is wrong-data-structure and the two flags should unify into a single per-descriptor enum, Hickey says detailed_metric should have grown a per-level scope, Torvalds calls it P2 polish, and Knuth/Liskov/Dijkstra mostly treat it as a separate spec/precedence problem rather than a unification opportunity. The panel verdict is REFUSED / NEEDS-WORK in current form: fix the shared-state mutation, gate the override on a real predicate (the valueToMetric flag, not string inequality), drop the dead NewRateLimit/NewStats allocation, collapse the parallel builders, and add concurrent and cardinality tests before this lands.
